title: Transform query results with the TestData data source

blocks.content:
Transformations change query results before Grafana displays them in a panel. You can calculate a single value from a series, rename columns, or combine results from multiple queries.

Grafana stores query results in data frames: tables of rows and columns, where each column is called a field. In this guide, you will create a dashboard and use sample data from the **TestData** data source to try two transformations.

blocks.title: Before you start
blocks.content: You need permission to create dashboards. If your Grafana instance does not already have a TestData data source, an administrator must add one in the first section.
Add a TestData data source to generate sample data, or skip this section if one already exists.
Open the list of data source types under **Connections**.
blocks.tooltip: Generate sample data without connecting to an external service or entering credentials.

blocks.content: Click **TestData** to create the data source.
blocks.tooltip: Grafana creates the data source immediately.

blocks.content: You now have a data source that generates sample data for your panel.
Create a new dashboard and add a panel that queries three sample time series.

blocks.title: Create a dashboard and query sample data

blocks.content: Create a new dashboard, add a panel, and open the panel editor.

steps.tooltip: Use an unsaved dashboard to try the transformations.
Add an empty panel to the new dashboard.
Configure the panel query and transformations.

blocks.tooltip: Select the source of sample data for this panel.

blocks.content: Set **Series count** to `3`, then run the query.

steps.tooltip: Generate three time series to compare before and after the transformation.
Display the three time series in the panel preview.

blocks.content: Your new dashboard has a panel with three sample time series from one query.
Apply **Reduce** to calculate a summary value for each series and inspect the result in **Table view**.
Click **Transformations** next to **Queries**; if your editor has a **Transformations** sidebar section instead, skip this step.
blocks.tooltip: Configure how Grafana processes the query results.

steps.tooltip: Choose a transformation to apply to the query results.
Filter the list to find the transformation.
Calculate a summary value for each series.

blocks.content: Turn on **Table view** to inspect the transformed results.
blocks.tooltip: Compare each series name with its calculated value.

blocks.content: You used **Reduce** to calculate a summary value for each series.
Add **Organize fields by name** to see how a second transformation uses the results of the first.
Add **Organize fields by name** after Reduce.

steps.tooltip: Choose another transformation to process the current results.
Find the option for renaming, reordering, and hiding columns.
Work with the columns produced by the previous transformation.

blocks.content:
You added **Organize fields by name** after **Reduce**, so it lists the columns produced by that first transformation.

Each transformation receives the results of the one before it, so their order matters. Try renaming a column in **Organize fields by name**, then check the result in **Table view**.

To explore further, try **Filter data by values** to remove rows that match a condition, or **Add field from calculation** to calculate a new column from existing values.
